title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Pascagoula, MS: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Pascagoula shipyard, icebreaker, refinery and fabrication inspectors: Navy rules, Part C code choice, Part B and eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Pascagoula: Six Days for Mississippi Gulf Coast Shipyard, Refinery and Fabrication Welding Inspectors
html:
Pascagoula is a shipbuilding town with a refinery beside it. Ingalls Shipbuilding, the largest manufacturing employer in Mississippi, builds destroyers and amphibious warships and has delivered ten cutters to the Coast Guard. Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding is building the Coast Guard's first new heavy polar icebreaker in decades. And Chevron's Pascagoula refinery is the biggest of the state's three, according to the US Energy Information Administration. Together they keep a great many welders, fitters and inspectors busy, and they weld to very different rule books.

Atlantis NDT runs a six-day course that prepares Mississippi Gulf Coast candidates for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination: shipyard welders, shipfitters and pipefitters, refinery and turnaround craft workers, QA and QC staff, NDT technicians and production engineers. The American Welding Society administers the examination and issues the certification. Candidates apply to AWS one by one and must each meet its education, experience and vision requirements. The course has not been approved or endorsed by AWS, and Atlantis does not see AWS examination content. There is no Atlantis classroom in Pascagoula. You can study the six days online at your own pace with an instructor answering your questions, an employer can have them delivered at its yard or plant for a group, or you can book one-to-one sessions, online or in person at a location agreed when you book. The course outline for each day is on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

Two rule books on one stretch of coast

Military ships are built to the shipbuilding contract, which calls up Navy technical publications and military standards for fabrication, welding, inspection and nondestructive testing. Refinery piping, structural fabrication and most commercial work are built to civilian codes from ASME, AWS and API. A welding inspector on the Mississippi coast can spend a career in one world or move between them, and the CWI matters differently in each. Understanding that split before you choose a Part C book saves a lot of wasted study.

Picture a pipe welder who spends one year on a destroyer's piping systems under the Navy fabrication document and the yard's qualified procedures, then joins a refinery turnaround crew working to ASME B31.3 and the owner's specification. The welding skill carries over almost entirely. The paperwork does not: different qualification records, different acceptance criteria, different people signing. A welding inspector who understands the common ground, and knows exactly where the two systems part company, is useful in both places, and the CWI syllabus is built around that common ground.

Ingalls Shipbuilding: destroyers, amphibious ships and a new frigate

HII's Ingalls fact sheet puts the yard's workforce at more than 11,000 people. Ingalls builds Flight III Arleigh Burke-class (DDG 51) destroyers and has delivered 36 ships of the class, is the sole builder of the San Antonio-class (LPD 17) amphibious transport docks, now in Flight II, and has two America-class (LHA 6) amphibious assault ships under construction, with a fifth, LHA 10, awarded. It has delivered ten Legend-class National Security Cutters to the Coast Guard and is modernizing the Zumwalt-class destroyers USS Zumwalt and Lyndon B. Johnson. In December 2025 the Navy selected Ingalls to design and build its FF(X) frigate, and a lead yard support contract followed in April 2026.

Ship construction at that scale is welding at every stage: plate and stiffener panels, units and grand blocks, foundations, piping systems and outfitting. The yard also trains craft workers through the Ingalls Apprentice School, described further down this page.

Navy specifications and where a CWI fits

On Navy work, the contract decides which NAVSEA publications and military standards apply and in which editions. Two that shipyard welding and inspection staff meet often are S9074-AR-GIB-010/278, which covers fabrication welding and inspection for machinery, piping and pressure vessels, and T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, which covers nondestructive testing requirements. Those documents, together with the procedures the yard qualifies under them, decide who may inspect and accept Navy welds. None of them is a Part C option, and an AWS CWI does not stand in for the qualifications they require.

That does not make the credential irrelevant in a Navy yard. The CWI body of knowledge, from processes, joint design and welding symbols to metallurgy, distortion, discontinuities and qualification records, is the foundation the Navy documents build on, and many supervisors, QA staff and engineers hold it as proof of that foundation. It also travels. A shipyard welder who later moves to a fabrication shop, a refinery contractor or a commercial yard finds that the CWI is the credential those employers ask for by name. Treat it as a portable base, then learn the Navy documents that apply to your job from the yard's own training.

Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding and the Polar Security Cutter

Bollinger bought the former VT Halter Marine yard in Pascagoula in November 2022, and Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding is now building the Coast Guard's Polar Security Cutter, which the company calls the nation's first heavy polar icebreaker in nearly fifty years. The Coast Guard approved full production in spring 2025, and Bollinger anticipated completing the first ship by May 2030. The company said its Mississippi workforce had grown by more than 61 percent since the acquisition and its production roles by more than 178 percent, helped by its own workforce bootcamps.

Icebreaker hulls use thick, high-strength steel that rewards careful control of preheat, interpass temperature, fit-up and distortion, and an inspector who understands why those controls exist adds real value on the deck plates. As with the Navy programs, the contract specifies the rules for Coast Guard work, and the yard's procedures and quality plan decide who inspects.

The Chevron refinery: pressure piping next to the yards

The EIA's refinery capacity report for January 2026 lists Chevron's Pascagoula refinery at 356,440 barrels per calendar day of crude distillation capacity, out of 393,940 for all three Mississippi refineries. Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College counts the refinery among its regional partners. Refinery welding is pressure work: process piping is built and repaired to ASME B31.3 with procedures and welders qualified to ASME Section IX, and pressure vessel repairs follow the owner's inspection program under documents such as API 510. A CWI on a refinery contract typically checks material, fit-up and preheat, verifies welder qualifications against the procedure, carries out visual acceptance and makes sure the required NDT and pressure tests happen and are recorded.

Many Gulf Coast craft workers move between the yards and refinery turnarounds over a career, which is one reason the CWI is worth having on this coast: it is recognized on both sides of the fence. Background reading: ASME B31.3 and ASME Section IX.

Choosing Part C on the Mississippi coast

Part C is open book, 50 to 65 questions on one code you choose from the AWS list. Navy publications and classification society rules are not on that list, so shipyard candidates pick the civilian code closest to the work they expect to do next.

If most of your future work isChoose for Part CExam edition AWS listed in November 2026
Structural and commercial fabrication, modules, platforms and steel structuresAWS D1.12020
Refinery and chemical plant piping, turnarounds and power plant pipingASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.32023, 2024 and 2024
Pipeline construction and tie-insAPI 110422nd edition
Aluminum fabrication, including aluminum boat and superstructure workAWS D1.22014

If you are torn between D1.1 and the ASME option, ask where you want to be working in five years. Shipyard candidates heading for structural fabrication or a commercial yard usually take D1.1; those eyeing refinery contractors take the ASME option. For background, read AWS D1.1 and the guide to WPS, PQR and WPQ records.

From apprentice to inspector

Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College, based in Perkinston and serving George, Harrison, Jackson and Stone counties, runs its maritime training at the Haley Reeves Barbour Maritime Training Academy in Pascagoula. The college is the Department of Labor sponsor of the Ingalls Apprentice School, a partnership MARAD's 2026 overview puts at 70 years, with more than 600 apprentices across 14 craft disciplines, among them welder, pipe welder, shipfitter and pipe fitter. An apprentice who completes an approved program can receive 30 semester hours toward an Apprentice Associate of Applied Science in Maritime Technology, and applicants apply through Ingalls rather than through the college.

How AWS treats apprenticeship and shipyard experience is its decision, so the application should spell the work out. Three hypothetical candidates show the kind of question that arises:

  • A welder who completed the Ingalls apprenticeship and then spent three more years welding hull units. Completed trade or vocational training puts the AWS requirement at four years of welding-related experience, and this record should reach it if AWS accepts the apprenticeship years and every period is confirmed.
  • A shipfitter with a high school diploma and six years of fit-up and tack welding. The diploma line asks for five years, and the open question is how much of the fitting work AWS regards as welding-related, which a detailed description helps answer.
  • A production engineer with an engineering bachelor's degree and two years supervising welded construction at a yard. That degree falls under the AWS line asking for two years, documented with the procedures, inspection plans and weld records the engineer handled.

Everyone also needs a passed vision test, recorded on the AWS visual acuity form and recent enough to count on exam day. The CWI requirements guide sets out the full rules, and candidates below the CWI thresholds can consider the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) first.

The AWS Pascagoula Section and District 9

Pascagoula has its own AWS section, part of District 9. In 2026 it reported on the South Mississippi Welding Competition, held on May 1 at MGCCC's George County Center in Lucedale with about 80 students, faculty and industry partners, and on the District 9 conference at Auburn University on May 30. In March 2026 the Mobile Section hosted a joint meeting of the Mobile, Auburn, Birmingham and Pascagoula sections in Loxley, Alabama. Section events are a good way to meet working CWIs and, sometimes, the supervisors who can confirm your experience.

Part B from the Gulf Coast

AWS gives Parts A and C by computer at Prometric centers and runs Part B, the practical, at its own seminar locations. The AWS list of CWI training locations in late 2026 had no Mississippi entry, but New Orleans and Birmingham were on it, with Houston and Tampa among the other Gulf-region sites. Pick a session from the AWS seminar and exam schedule, then work back: US applications close six weeks before the Part B date, and each part requires at least 72 percent. Allow for travel and a possible retake; the CWI exam cost calculator helps you budget.

The practical hands you AWS's tools, specimens and documents and asks 46 questions. Shipyard candidates often measure well but lose marks by judging against the yard's criteria out of habit, so practise reading the supplied procedure or acceptance criteria first and comparing each gauge reading against those.

Preparing around a shipyard schedule

Yard and refinery schedules rarely leave a free week. The online format turns the six days into a study plan you can work through on evenings and days off, with written questions answered by the instructor and timed practice papers to show your readiness. A sensible order is welding symbols and terminology first, then metallurgy, testing and discontinuities, then the code book, leaving the timed papers until the last stretch before Part A. One-to-one sessions, online or in person, suit a candidate who needs concentrated help on one part.

A group course for a yard or contractor

A shipyard subcontractor, fabrication shop or turnaround contractor preparing several people can have the six days delivered at its own site under the corporate format. The group practises with its own weld samples and gauges, and the code sessions follow the book most of them will choose, typically D1.1 for fabricators and the ASME option for pipe crews. The employer picks the weeks, which matters around launch dates, sea trials and refinery outages. Every participant still makes an individual AWS application, backed by a personal vision record and experience evidence.

After certification

A CWI is valid for nine years, with renewals at years three and six and recertification at year nine through professional development hours, retaking Part B, or the AWS Certified Radiographic Interpreter credential. Coast CWIs who stay in refinery work often add an API individual certification such as API 510 or API 570; Atlantis offers self-paced API exam preparation, and API administers those examinations and certifies inspectors. Others add NDT methods, certified by the employer under its written practice; Atlantis provides training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, including VT Level 2, UT Level 2 and MT Level 2, with the employer certifying afterward.

Local pages: NDT training in Pascagoula, maritime NDT training in Pascagoula, refining NDT training in Pascagoula, and CWI exam prep in Mobile, New Orleans and Birmingham.

Enquiring from Pascagoula

Tell us the format, the number of candidates, the Part C book each expects to take and the Part B session you have in mind. Employers should add the site and the weeks that work around launches, trials or turnarounds. If an apprenticeship or shipyard record leaves you unsure how AWS will count it, describe it and we will tell you what to confirm with AWS. The format you choose is quoted on request, and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Pascagoula?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Pascagoula. You can take the six days online, have them delivered at your employer's yard or plant for a group, or book them one-to-one online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

faq.q: Does a CWI replace Navy inspection qualifications at a shipyard?
faq.a: No. On Navy work the contract and the NAVSEA publications it calls up, with the yard's procedures, decide who may inspect and accept welds. The CWI is a portable base of welding knowledge, not a substitute for those qualifications.

faq.q: Can I use a NAVSEA publication or classification society rules for Part C?
faq.a: No. Neither is on the AWS list of Part C books. Shipyard candidates usually take AWS D1.1 for structural and fabrication work or the ASME option if they expect to move into refinery piping.

faq.q: Which Part C book suits work at the Chevron Pascagoula refinery?
faq.a: Usually the ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, because refinery piping and welder qualification are written around those documents.

faq.q: Does an Ingalls apprenticeship count toward CWI experience?
faq.a: AWS decides. A completed apprenticeship may support the trade or vocational line of the AWS table, and the welding-related work during and after it must be documented with dates, duties and someone who can confirm them.

faq.q: Where can I take Part B from the Mississippi coast?
faq.a: The AWS list of CWI training locations in late 2026 had no Mississippi entry but included New Orleans and Birmingham, with Houston and Tampa also listed. Check the AWS seminar and exam schedule for Part B dates.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Pascagoula?
faq.a: Yes. The AWS Pascagoula Section is part of District 9 and posts its events on sections.aws.org, including the South Mississippi Welding Competition held at MGCCC in 2026.

faq.q: Is the course approved by AWS?
faq.a: No. The course carries no AWS approval or endorsement, and nobody at Atlantis has seen AWS examination content. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: How do I get a quote from Pascagoula?
faq.a: Use the enquiry link on this page to send the format, how many candidates there are and the Part C book. We prepare a quote on request for the chosen format and reply within one business day.
